subject: society
topic: Open offices made people talk to each other less
angle: Open office designs can cause people to socially withdraw from face-to-face interaction in favor of electronic communication.
title: The Architecture of Isolation

hooks.text: Why are you talking to your screen instead of your coworkers?
You thought open offices would bring people together.
You are hiding behind your email in a room full of people.
A row of desks. A series of pings.

reveal.headline: Open offices link to social withdrawal.
reveal.body: Open office architecture appears to trigger a natural human response to withdraw from coworkers. Instead of face-to-face interaction, people interact over email and instant messages.

explain.headline: The architecture of your workspace matters.
explain.body: Research shows that open designs are linked to a decrease in personal interaction. Workplaces can be designed to balance collaboration and concentration, but open plans often lead to electronic communication.

matters.headline: Your digital presence is a defense.
matters.body: That may be why you reach for your keyboard instead of looking up. The physical space you work in might be driving you to isolate yourself behind a screen.

example.headline: A message instead of a nod.
example.body: You sit at your desk. A coworker walks past. You do not look up. You type a message to them instead of speaking aloud. You stay in your chair. The screen stays lit.

question.headline: When was the last time you spoke to the person next to you?

stat.label: human response to open office architecture

claims.text: Open architecture appeared to trigger a natural human response to socially withdraw from officemates and interact instead over email and IM.
claims.quote: In short, rather than prompting increasingly vibrant face-to-face collaboration, open architecture appeared to trigger a natural human response to socially withdraw from officemates and interact instead over email and IM.

claims.text: The best-performing offices implemented active and biophilic design, prioritized overall ergonomics and different spaces designed to support a variety of work-related activities.
claims.quote: The best-performing offices implemented active and biophilic design, prioritized overall ergonomics and different spaces designed to support a variety of work-related activities.

claims.text: Workplaces can be successfully designed to facilitate the seemingly conflicting requirements of supporting both collaboration and concentration.

verdict: The evidence shows that open office architectures are linked to a decrease in face-to-face interaction and an increase in electronic interaction.
caveat: The research is limited by a lack of direct empirical research on how human interaction patterns change as a result of these architectural changes.
caption:
Open office designs are linked to a decrease in face-to-face interaction. 

Research shows that these architectures appear to trigger a natural human response to withdraw socially and favor electronic communication. Note that research is limited by a lack of direct empirical data on how these patterns change. 

Do you find yourself typing more than talking today?
